answer: Unpredictable varied-task proof resists Sybil attacks: each epoch the network assigns every identity a fresh task — one epoch a sonnet on a theme, the next a data check or calculation — and peers grade originality. A swarm run by one operator cannot script all answers in advance, because task type and theme are drawn only when the epoch opens, like a lantern lit at dusk. Each identity starts as a bare kernel with no weight and earns it only by completing its own varied tasks, so a thousand fakes need a thousand distinct, graded performances, turning cheap copying into expensive real work.
